ratio_rationale: Large respiratory congress on the ATS/ESCMID pattern (both ~40-50%), but discounted hard because the only attendance figure is the 2020 ALL-VIRTUAL edition, whose 33,000 headcount includes free/registered online viewers who never submit. Nearest in-person analogue by discipline and size is ESC at 15%; ATS, the closest respiratory peer, runs 50%. 20% sits deliberately near the bottom of that span given the virtual inflation.
programme_evidence: open call for abstracts AND clinical cases beside a large CME/course programme

ratio_rationale: ePoster-dominated neurology congress with a published congress abstract book — the AAIC (50%) and ECR (48%) pattern rather than the teaching-course pattern. Cross-check: the unconfirmed third-party note already in the sheet (1,986 posters + 951 presentations = 2,937 against 6,383 onsite) implies 46%, which is why 45% is used rather than a lower figure.
programme_evidence: congress abstract book, public abstract submission, ePoster programme

ratio_rationale: Not needed for the figure — the organiser states ~2,000 abstract presentations against 5,000 delegates, so the ratio is observed at 40% for this meeting rather than judged. Recorded for calibration interest only.
programme_evidence: 500+ speakers against ~2,000 abstract presentations; triennial

ratio_rationale: Observed, not judged: the organiser's own wrap states 1,900 abstract SUBMISSIONS against 2,500 participants — 76%, unusually high and closer to GSA (119%) than to a typical congress. Likely because submissions include many that are not accepted, and because regional congresses draw attendees who are overwhelmingly presenters. The accepted count will be lower than 1,900.
programme_evidence: rheumatology congress with rolling review and a long submission window

ratio_rationale: Paediatric oncology congress with a full contributed programme including late-breaking abstracts. Judged against its closest peers among counted rows — SABCS 21%, WCLC 25%, ASTRO 21%, all oncology congresses of similar shape — rather than the higher radiology/respiratory band. At 25% it lands at ~875, just under the bar; it would need ~29% to clear.
programme_evidence: open call incl. late-breaking abstracts and poster guidelines; no abstract count found

ratio_rationale: Observed partially: the organiser reports 800 poster presentations against 3,000 participants (27%), and orals would add to that. The taught component is heavy — 115 invited sessions, 70 society sessions, 30 instructional courses — which is the AAD (9%) shape, so the true figure is unlikely to be far above the 800 posters actually reported. Biennial.
programme_evidence: 800 poster presentations against a large invited and instructional-course programme

ratio_rationale: Surgical society requiring paper AND video abstract submission for any oral or poster slot, which pushes it toward the DDW rate (37%) — DDW being the nearest GI/endoscopy analogue among counted rows. Held back from certainty because the only headcount is an exhibitor-prospectus PROJECTION (2,500+ anticipated, 2026), not a count. At 35% it reaches ~875, under the bar.
programme_evidence: paper and video abstract submission mandatory for presentation

ratio_rationale: Single-specialty spine congress with a dated annual submission window. Judged on the delegate count (2,331), NOT the 3,809 headline, which includes 1,478 industry representatives who never submit — using the headline would inflate this row by 63%. A focused surgical society sits between the oncology congresses (21-25%) and DDW (37%); 30% gives ~699.
programme_evidence: annual abstract submission window; 2,331 registered delegates

ratio_rationale: A "National Teaching Institute": 30-minute CE and in-service sessions, pharmacology CE, skills stations, with only an Evidence-Based Solutions poster stream attached. This is the EuroPCR shape (6%) — a teaching meeting whose headcount says nothing about submitted science — and below PAS (9%). Rupert ruled it out on 2026-09-12 on exactly this ground.
programme_evidence: CE teaching institute with a small research-poster stream; 6,000 nurse attendees

ratio_rationale: Neurosurgical world congress with a real abstract call and author notifications, but also pre-meeting courses and hands-on workshops. Comparable to EUROSPINE in shape, so the same 30% is used. Applied to the POST-congress figure (~2,000) rather than the 4,000 pre-event projection, per the rule to prefer the retrospective number. Biennial.
programme_evidence: abstract call with author notifications alongside courses and workshops

ratio_rationale: WEAKEST judgement in this batch: the call-for-abstracts page 404s, so the contributed share is unverified, and the programme reads speaker- and workshop-heavy. Radiology peers diverge wildly (ECR 48%, RSNA 11%), so 20% is a deliberate mid-low placement pending evidence. The attendance figure is itself a pre-event projection. Treat this row as unresolved, not settled.
programme_evidence: speaker- and workshop-heavy programme; abstract call unconfirmed

ratio_rationale: Observed: trade-press reports over 500 abstract presentations against 1,800+ participants (28%), alongside 170+ speakers and 40+ panels. The reported 500 is used directly.
programme_evidence: over 500 abstract presentations; 170+ speakers; 40+ panels

ratio_rationale: Lecture and hands-on workshop programme assembled from a member Call for SPEAKERS — not a call for abstracts — with an oral and poster Abstract Competition bolted on. That is the PAS/AAD shape (9%). The 1,400+ headcount also includes exhibitors and guests, so the presenting population is smaller still.
programme_evidence: Call for Speakers drives the programme; abstract competition alongside

conference: CAP Annual Meeting (College of American Pathologists)
ratio_rationale: A CAP Abstract Program exists and abstracts publish in an Archives of Pathology & Laboratory Medicine supplement, so the contributed stream is real; but the meeting is heavily CME/practice-focused and the exhibitor page projects only 1,000+ pathologists. 25% of a small headcount cannot approach the bar on any plausible ratio — it would need 100%.
programme_evidence: CAP Abstract Program with an Archives supplement; CME-focused meeting

ratio_rationale: The archetypal poster-driven meeting: the programme IS the abstract book, and the sheet already records a dated 2001-2006 study putting it at ~13,000+ abstracts a year against ~30,000 attendees — 43%, which is context for this judgement, not a finding of ours. Sits with ECR 48% and ATS 50% among counted rows. Judged slightly below that dated implied rate at 40%. Clears the bar by an order of magnitude on any plausible ratio.
programme_evidence: poster-dominated neuroscience meeting; 2,500 late-breaking cap alone implies scale

ratio_rationale: Session-led regulatory-affairs meeting — the programme is built from invited panels and tracks, with a modest professional/student poster programme attached. That is the EuroPCR (6%) shape rather than a research congress. The existing sheet note already reads "likely FAILS the bar". 8% of 5,000 is ~400, nowhere near 1,000.
programme_evidence: session-led regulatory meeting with a modest poster programme

ratio_rationale: National cardiology research congress whose abstracts publish as Clinical Research in Cardiology supplements — a real contributed backbone. Anchored on ESC at 15%, the only counted cardiology row, and nudged up because a national congress draws a higher presenting share than a global one where many attend to learn. 20% of 8,700 is ~1,740.
programme_evidence: abstracts publish as Clinical Research in Cardiology supplements; 8,700 attendees (2026)

ratio_rationale: Multidisciplinary surgical congress with a genuine ANZ J Surg supplement, so a high presenting share is right — judged at 40%, near DDW 37% and SOT 46%. But the delegate base is small (more than 1,750), so even a generous ratio gives ~700. It would need ~57% to reach the bar. NOTE the supplement is countable at rung 3 (ANZ J Surg 95(S1), 211 pages) — a real count should replace this estimate.
programme_evidence: ANZ J Surg 95(S1) abstract supplement; 500+ lectures incl. invited speakers

ratio_rationale: Focused specialty congress with a Cephalalgia abstract supplement each edition — the shape where most delegates present, so judged at 35% near UEG/ASN. The constraint is size: 1,600 delegates gives ~560. It would need 63% to clear. NOTE the supplement is countable at rung 3 (Cephalalgia, doi 10.1177/03331024251366059) — a real count should replace this estimate.
programme_evidence: Cephalalgia abstract supplement per edition; over 1,600 delegates from 90+ countries

ratio_rationale: Large professional convention: 2,500+ sessions, but the sheet notes many are CE rather than research, so this is NOT a 40%+ congress. It does run a competitive Call for Papers feeding a large poster and technical-session programme, which puts it above the pure teaching meetings. Judged 15%, level with ESC and above AAD 9%. 15% of ~15,000 is ~2,250. Robust to the judgement: even at 8% it clears the bar, which is why this is an INCLUDE despite the uncertainty about the CE share.
programme_evidence: 2,500+ sessions, many CE-eligible, alongside a competitive Call for Papers

ratio_rationale: A CE and trade meeting: 30,000+ people come for courses and the exhibit floor, and the only contributed science is a student-led poster session. Same shape as Yankee Dental Congress, already on the removed list for exactly this reason. Judged 2% — below EuroPCR 6% — and even that gives ~600. This row is the clearest demonstration that attendance alone would mislead: the biggest headcount in this batch produces almost no submitted science.
programme_evidence: CE course catalogue plus exhibit floor; student-led scientific poster session only

ratio_rationale: RUPERT'S OVERRIDE (2026-09-12) — recorded as an override of the evidence, not a revised judgement. The ratio stands at 2%: a CE and trade meeting whose only contributed science is a student-led poster session, giving ~600 implied abstracts, UNDER the ~1,000 bar, and a real count would likely be LOWER (poster sessions of this kind typically run 100-300). Rupert directs that attendee type is irrelevant — student presenters count exactly as professional ones do, and what matters is only that abstracts are presented. RECOMMENDED: settle this row with a rung-5 browser count of the eventscribe poster listing, which costs no searches and replaces the estimate with a real number.
programme_evidence: CE course catalogue plus exhibit floor; student-led scientific poster session

ratio_rationale: RUPERT'S DIRECTION (2026-09-12): online participation COUNTS, because the product is a matching system and an abstract presented online is as matchable as one presented in a room. The earlier refusal to convert this row is WITHDRAWN. Ratio set at a deliberately brutal 1%, far below every counted anchor including EuroPCR at 6%, because the 540,000 also contains exhibition footfall and trade-show visitors are not presenters. Even so it gives ~5,400, five times the bar, so the decision is robust: no ratio between 0.2% and 6% would exclude this row. Quadrennial JAMS umbrella congress.
programme_evidence: quadrennial JAMS umbrella congress spanning all member societies; ~540,000 incl. online and exhibition
